findings.F1: The tested result points the way the idea predicts but falls short of the bar. Over all folds, short cases had a mean unusual 7-day move of +1.06 % (day-clustered t 1.41, 441 cases on 350 days, strength 0.075). In folds B and C alone, the 7-day grid cases in the situation had a mean of +2.29 % (t 1.44 with the cases of one day together, 228 cases on 86 days, strength 0.14).
findings.F2: The effect is mixed across periods and coins.
findings.F3: The further fall is graded by the raw 30-day efficiency ratio.
findings.F4: The plan's forecast standardises ER against its own past 60 values, which correlates only 0.68 with the raw ratio. That may be why the full-data supporting check failed (stronger minus weaker −0.56 %). In folds B and C the forecast terciles were still graded: +0.33 %, +2.76 %, +4.41 % from weak to strong forecast.
findings.F5: Weekly falls outside the situation show no continuation (mean −0.19 %, t −0.26, 361 cases), so what the move follows is the choppy 30-day path.
findings.F6: The 7-day horizon is where the effect shows: −0.66 % over 3 days (t −1.01), +2.29 % over 7 days and +2.72 % over 14 days (t 1.74, plain t, 214 cases).
findings.F7: The total move per case over all folds was +0.17 %, 0.9 times the 0.19 % cost of a trade. The unusual move was 5.5 times that cost, so only a clearer, larger effect would let a book pay.

ideas.same-idea-on: instruments: BTC, ETH, LTC, XMR, XRP, ZEC, ADA, DOGE, LINK, TRX, UNI, AAVE, AVAX, SOL, INJ, NEAR, SUI, TAO, ONDO; bar: 1d; period: folds A, B, C, D
ideas.name: choppy falls, more coins
ideas.idea: When a coin has fallen over the past 7 days while its past 30 days were choppy and agitated, with large daily swings both ways and little net progress, it tends to keep falling over the next 7 days. The less net progress the coin made over those 30 days relative to the path it travelled, the larger that further fall.
ideas.consequence: A trader should refuse to buy weekly dips in choppy agitated markets, and may lean short after them, most of all when the 30-day path has gone nowhere.

ideas.idea: When a coin has fallen over the past 7 days, it tends to keep falling over the next 7 days, and the less net progress its past 30 days made relative to the path its price travelled, the larger that further fall.
ideas.consequence: A trader should refuse to buy a weekly dip that comes after a month of going nowhere, and may lean short on it, more so the more directionless that month was.
ideas.name: weekly falls after directionless months
